nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The NF was sonicated successively with 0.5 M H2SO4, deionized water and ethanol for 15 min to remove impurities.
nodes.source_text: The NF was sonicated successively with 0.5 M H2SO4, deionized water and ethanol for 15 min to remove impurities.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal CrOOH/NF
nodes.procedure: Cr(NO3)3·9H2O (2.5 mmol) and CO(NH2)2 (25 mmol) were dissolved in 80 mL of deionized water and stirred for 15 min to obtain a clear solution. Then the resulting solution was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-line stainless steel autoclave. The pretreated NF (3 cm × 3 cm) was placed obliquely in the autoclave and kept at 120 °C for 12 h. After cooling to room temperature naturally, the obtained product was washed with deionized water for several times and dried at room temperature for further use.

nodes.name: Drop casting Re precursor
nodes.procedure: NH₄ReO₄ (0.15 mmol) was dissolved in a mixed solution containing 200 μL deionized water, 200 μL ethanol and 10 μL Nafion and ultrasonicated for 20 min. The Nafion is used as a binding agent. Then the mixture solution was pipetted onto the surface of CrOOH/NF (1 cm × 1 cm) to obtain the Cr-Re species/NF.

nodes.name: Phosphating treatment
nodes.procedure: Two pieces of Cr-Re species/NF (1 cm × 1 cm) and 1.0 g of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O were placed on the downstream and upstream of the tube furnace, respectively. Subsequently, the tube furnace was heated slowly to 350 °C (5 °C min⁻¹) under N₂ flow (20 sccm) for 2 h. After natural cooling to room temperature, the yellow phosphate formed at the top of the quartz tube adhered to the surface of the catalysts (Fig. S1), therefore the catalysts were washed with deionized water to get rid of the phosphate contaminate. The prepared sample was named as CrP-Re₂P/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of CrP-Re₂P/NF align with CrP (JCPDS: 29-0456) and Re₂P (JCPDS: 17-0391), confirming the two major crystalline structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1d the diffraction peaks of CrP-Re₂P/NF align with the CrP (JCPDS: 290,456) and Re₂P (JCPDS: 17-0391), indicating the two major crystalline structures are CrP and Re₂P.

nodes.characterization_summary: CrP-Re₂P/NF exhibits loose and porous sponge-like materials covering the NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface of NF was covered with a large amount of loose and porous sponge-like materials, when the precursor of Re was loaded on the CrOOH/NF (12 h) surface and followed by phosphate treatment (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniformly distributed nanoparticles with average size of 1.64 nm on CrP-Re₂P/NF flakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image of the ultrasonically stripped catalyst fragments shows that there are uniformly distributed nanoparticles on the surface of the flakes (Fig. 2b), and the average size of the particles is about 1.64 nm (inset Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED reveals lattice spacings of 0.203 nm and 0.181 nm corresponding to CrP (210) and Re₂P (114) crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) in Fig. 2c reveals that the lattice spacing of 0.203 nm and 0.181 nm correspond to the CrP (210) and Re₂P (114) crystal planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms Re₂P (114, 203) planes at 0.181 nm and 0.214 nm, and CrP (210) plane at 0.203 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main components of the particles are attributed to the (114) and (203) crystal planes of Re₂P species with lattice spacings of 0.181 and 0.214 nm (Fig. 2d). In addition, the (210) crystal plane of the CrP component with a lattice spacing of 0.203 nm was also observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM elemental mappings show Cr, Re, and P uniformly distributed throughout CrP-Re₂P/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image and corresponding elemental mappings display that Cr, Re and P are uniformly distributed throughout the CrP-Re₂P/NF (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms presence of Cr, Re, P in CrP-Re₂P/NF catalyst with Ni from substrate and O from surface oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometer (EDS) analysis of CrP-Re₂P/NF catalyst is showed in Fig. 2f. The Ni peak is attributed to the nickel foam, and the O peak can be attributed to the oxidation of the catalyst surface when exposed to air.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measures metal loadings: CrP-Re₂P/NF (24.4 mg/cm²), CrP/NF (24.2 mg/cm²), Re₂P/NF (18.6 mg/cm²) as shown in Table S1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The catalyst loading of the CrP-Re₂P, CrP, and Re₂P on NF surface are approximately 24.4, 24.2 and 18.6 mg cm⁻², respectively, and are summarized in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of CrP-Re₂P/NF shows Cr 2p peaks at 575.3/584.6 eV (Cr-P), 578.0/587.2 eV (Cr-O), 580.9/590.3 eV (Cr oxides); Re 4f₇/₂ at 41.6 eV and 4f₅/₂ at 43.4 eV (Re-P) with binding energy shifts indicating charge transfer between CrP and Re₂P; P 2p₃/₂ at 129.6 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 130.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cr 2p region of CrP-Re₂P/NF presents three major groups, in which the deconvoluted peaks at 575.3 (Cr 2p3/2) and 584.6 (Cr 2p) eV are attributed to Cr-P... Deconvolution of high-resolution spectra in the Re 4f region shows the presence of the doublet Re 4f₇/₂ (41.6 eV) and 4f₅/₂ (43.4 eV)... The P 2p of CrP-Re₂P/NF mainly includes P 2p₃/₂ (129.6 eV) and P 2p₁/₂ (130.5 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines catalyst compositions and metal loadings: CrP-Re₂P/NF (24.4 mg/cm²), CrP/NF (24.2 mg/cm²), Re₂P/NF (18.6 mg/cm²) summarized in Tables S2-S3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was used to calculate the final composition of the catalyst... ICP-MS measured different catalysts loading are shown in Table S2. The chemical formulas of the CrP-Re₂P/NF catalysts with different Re loadings are summarized in Table S3.
